pick.headline: Civil Guards seize Spain's parliament in failed coup
pick.summary: On February 23, 1981, Lieutenant Colonel Antonio Tejero led Civil Guards into the Spanish parliament and held the deputies hostage; the coup collapsed after King Juan Carlos denounced it on television.
pick.significance: The failure of the '23-F' coup consolidated Spain's young democracy.
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of February 24, 1981, carried Moscow TASS, citing EFE, on about 200 Civil Guards under Lieutenant Colonel Tejero, "known by his Francoist views", storming the Spanish parliament during the vote on Calvo Sotelo, and General Milans del Bosch declaring emergency in Valencia.

alternates.headline: Military coup in Thailand
alternates.summary: On February 23, 1991, Thailand's military seized power and detained Prime Minister Chatichai Choonhavan.
alternates.significance: The coup interrupted an elected government and led to the bloody protests of May 1992.
alternates.fbis: The East Asia Daily Report of February 25, 1991, carried Tokyo KYODO on Japan's reaction to the military coup in Thailand: officials said ties would not be affected and that Japan, Thailand's main aid donor, was unlikely to follow the United States in suspending aid.
